name_note: Amygdalobacter is a recently named genus; its species A. indicium is the cultured representative of the organism long referred to in the literature as BVAB2.

sentences.text: Amygdalobacter is a genus of obligately anaerobic, Gram-positive, non-motile coccobacilli in the family Oscillospiraceae, described from four isolates from the female genital tract.
Its species Amygdalobacter indicium was proposed for a strain whose 16S rRNA gene was 99.4% similar to the uncultured clone known as Bacterial Vaginosis Associated Bacterium 2, or BVAB2.

In a study combining a sexually-inexperienced university population and a sexually-active clinic population, BVAB2 was one of four candidate organisms independently associated with bacterial vaginosis by multivariable analysis.
The same study reported that BVAB2 was rare or absent in sexually-unexposed women, with increasing odds of detection at higher levels of sexual activity or more lifetime partners.
A separate study reported that women who later developed recurrent bacterial vaginosis had greater concentrations of BVAB2 at initial diagnosis than women who stayed cured.
